# Command reference

Every command and option of `modelbump`, as `--help` shows them. New to
ModelBump? Start with the [tutorial](tutorial.md).

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`modelbump scan`](#modelbump-scan) | Find the LLM model IDs in a repository's code and config, and how urgent each is. |
| [`modelbump check`](#modelbump-check) | Look up one model ID in the retirement registry. |
| [`modelbump bump`](#modelbump-bump) | Change a model ID to a new one wherever the code uses it (a dry run by default). |
| [`modelbump bump-all`](#modelbump-bump-all) | Bump every model the code uses that is retired or shuts down soon (Dependabot-style). |
| [`modelbump prompts`](#modelbump-prompts) | List the LLM calls in Python code, with each call's model and prompt template. |
| [`modelbump cases`](#modelbump-cases) | Find test inputs for each LLM call: from the app's own tests and code, then generated. |
| [`modelbump suite`](#modelbump-suite) | Write a suite file: every complete test case, with its messages and its oracle. |
| [`modelbump test`](#modelbump-test) | Run a suite on the old and the new model and decide each test case. |
| [`modelbump oracles`](#modelbump-oracles) | Show how each LLM call's answers will be checked: JSON, label or free text. |
| [`modelbump ask`](#modelbump-ask) | Send prompts to a model and print the answers (to try the runner). |
| [`modelbump models`](#modelbump-models) | List the models pulled into Ollama, with the digest that pins each one. |
| [`modelbump cache info`](#modelbump-cache-info) | Show where the cache is and how much it holds. |
| [`modelbump cache clear`](#modelbump-cache-clear) | Delete every stored answer. |
| [`modelbump repair show`](#modelbump-repair-show) | Show what a patch changes in each test case, without asking any model. |
| [`modelbump repair propose`](#modelbump-repair-propose) | Ask a model for candidate patches for every call with a REGRESSED case (ADR 0063). |
| [`modelbump repair run`](#modelbump-repair-run) | Screen the candidate patches, confirm the best on fresh answers, keep only safe ones. |
| [`modelbump judge sheet`](#modelbump-judge-sheet) | Write a blind sheet of judged answers for you to label PASS or FAIL. |
| [`modelbump judge agreement`](#modelbump-judge-agreement) | How often the judge agrees with your labels, and pass rates corrected for it. |
| [`modelbump judge probes`](#modelbump-judge-probes) | Break reference answers on purpose, judge them, and write a blind sheet to check. |
| [`modelbump judge probe-check`](#modelbump-judge-probe-check) | Which kinds of broken answer the judge catches, checked against your labels. |
| [`modelbump stats item`](#modelbump-stats-item) | Compare pass counts of the old and new model on one test case. |
| [`modelbump stats simulate`](#modelbump-stats-simulate) | Pretend two models answer one test case, and stop as soon as the verdict is clear. |

## modelbump scan

Find the LLM model IDs in a repository's code and config, and how urgent each is.

```text
modelbump scan [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `PATH` | Folder or file to scan. | `.` |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--soon-days` | Mark a model RETIRING_SOON when it shuts down within this many days. | `90` |
| `--fail-within` | Exit with code 1 if a model is retired or shuts down within this many days. |  |
| `--today` | Check as if today were this day (YYYY-MM-DD), to replay the past. |  |
| `--format` | Report format: text, json or sarif. | `text` |
| `--exclude` | Skip paths matching this pattern, e.g. 'tests' or '*.ipynb'. Repeat for more. |  |
| `--skip-comments`, `--no-skip-comments` | Leave out IDs that only describe a model: comments, docstrings, sentences and price tables. | off |
| `--skip-tests`, `--no-skip-tests` | Leave out test files and test folders. | off |
| `--output` | Write the report to this file instead of the screen. |  |

## modelbump check

Look up one model ID in the retirement registry.

```text
modelbump check MODEL_ID
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `MODEL_ID` | Model ID, e.g. claude-3-haiku-20240307. | required |

## modelbump bump

Change a model ID to a new one wherever the code uses it (a dry run by default).

With --open-pr, the change goes to a new branch and a pull request whose description is the evidence report.

```text
modelbump bump [OPTIONS] OLD [PATH]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `OLD` | Model ID to move away from, e.g. gpt-4o-mini. | required |
| `PATH` | Folder or file to change. | `.` |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--to` | Model ID to move to. Default: the replacement the registry suggests. |  |
| `--write`, `--no-write` | Change the files. Without it, only show what would change. | off |
| `--include-docs`, `--no-include-docs` | Also change comments, docstrings and sentences that name the model. | off |
| `--env` | Read the model from this environment variable, e.g. OPENAI_MODEL, with the new model as the default (Python code; also added to .env.example). |  |
| `--suite` | The suite that was tested (`modelbump suite`), added as evidence. |  |
| `--report` | The JSON test report (`modelbump test --format json`), added as evidence. |  |
| `--repairs` | The repair report (`modelbump repair run`): accepted repairs go into the code. |  |
| `--proposals` | The folder from `modelbump repair propose`, holding the accepted patches. |  |
| `--patch` | A patch file to write into the code instead of --repairs, e.g. one tested with `modelbump test --patch`. |  |
| `--exclude` | Skip paths matching this pattern, e.g. 'tests'. Repeat for more. |  |
| `--today` | Check the new model's retirement as if today were this day (YYYY-MM-DD). |  |
| `--pr-body` | Write the pull request description (the evidence report) to this file. |  |
| `--open-pr` | Write the files, commit them on a new branch, push, and open a pull request with gh. Needs a clean git working tree. | off |

## modelbump bump-all

Bump every model the code uses that is retired or shuts down soon (Dependabot-style).

```text
modelbump bump-all [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `PATH` | Folder to check and change. | `.` |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--within` | Bump models that are retired or shut down within this many days. | `90` |
| `--open-pr` | Open one pull request per model with gh. A model whose branch is already there is skipped, so running this on a schedule never opens duplicates. | off |
| `--exclude` | Skip paths matching this pattern, e.g. 'tests'. Repeat for more. |  |
| `--today` | Check as if today were this day (YYYY-MM-DD). |  |

## modelbump prompts

List the LLM calls in Python code, with each call's model and prompt template.

```text
modelbump prompts [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `PATH` | Folder or Python file to read. | `.` |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--model` | Only list the calls to this model ID, e.g. gpt-4o-mini. |  |
| `--format` | Report format: text or json. | `text` |
| `--exclude` | Skip paths matching this pattern, e.g. 'scripts'. Repeat for more. |  |
| `--skip-tests`, `--no-skip-tests` | Leave out test files and test folders. | off |
| `--output` | Write the report to this file instead of the screen. |  |

## modelbump cases

Find test inputs for each LLM call: from the app's own tests and code, then generated.

With --generate N, a model (local Qwen 2.5 by default) writes inputs for the calls that have fewer than N cases. Generated cases say which model wrote them.

```text
modelbump cases [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `PATH` | Folder or Python file to read. | `.` |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--model` | Only list the calls to this model ID, e.g. gpt-4o-mini. |  |
| `--format` | Report format: text or json. | `text` |
| `--exclude` | Do not list calls in paths matching this pattern. Repeat for more. |  |
| `--skip-tests`, `--no-skip-tests` | Do not list calls made in test files (their inputs are still read). | off |
| `--output` | Write the report to this file instead of the screen. |  |
| `--generate` | Have a model write inputs until each call with slots has this many cases. | `0` |
| `--generator` | The model that writes inputs, as endpoint/model. | `ollama/qwen2.5:7b` |
| `--budget-requests` | Stop after this many requests to the writer model. |  |

## modelbump suite

Write a suite file: every complete test case, with its messages and its oracle.

```text
modelbump suite [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `PATH` | Folder or Python file to read. | `.` |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--output` | Where to write the suite file. | `modelbump-suite.json` |
| `--model` | Only the calls to this model ID, e.g. gpt-4o-mini. |  |
| `--exclude` | Leave out calls in paths matching this pattern. Repeat for more. |  |
| `--skip-tests`, `--no-skip-tests` | Leave out calls made in test files (their inputs are still read). | off |
| `--generate` | Have a model write inputs until each call with slots has this many cases. | `0` |
| `--generator` | The model that writes inputs, as endpoint/model. | `ollama/qwen2.5:7b` |
| `--budget-requests` | Stop after this many requests to the writer model. |  |

## modelbump test

Run a suite on the old and the new model and decide each test case.

Exits with 1 when a case REGRESSED or could not be run, so CI can fail on it.

```text
modelbump test [OPTIONS] SUITE_FILE
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `SUITE_FILE` | The suite file from `modelbump suite`. | required |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--from` | The model the app uses now, as endpoint/model. | required |
| `--to` | The model to move to, as endpoint/model. | required |
| `--runs` | Answers per model per case (the most, for sequential). | `50` |
| `--reference` | Old-model answers per case that set the reference (not scored). | `3` |
| `--method` | fixed (k + BH), sequential (+ e-BH), or auto (by --runs, ADR 0047). | `auto` |
| `--from-think` | Reasoning effort for the --from model: none, low, medium or high. |  |
| `--to-think` | Reasoning effort for the --to model, e.g. none for Qwen 3. |  |
| `--temperature` | Sampling temperature for both models. | `0.7` |
| `--max-tokens` | Longest answer, in tokens. | `400` |
| `--judge` | The model that judges free-text answers, as endpoint/model. | `ollama/gemma3:12b` |
| `--no-judge` | Check free text with property checks only. | off |
| `--budget-requests` | Stop after this many requests (cached answers are free). |  |
| `--format` | Report format: text or json (every answer and score). | `text` |
| `--output` | Write the report to this file instead of the screen. |  |
| `--patch` | A patch file: the new model gets the patched prompts (ADR 0062). |  |

|---|---|---|
| `PATH` | Folder or Python file to read. | `.` |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--model` | Only list the calls to this model ID, e.g. gpt-4o-mini. |  |
| `--format` | Report format: text or json. | `text` |
| `--exclude` | Skip paths matching this pattern, e.g. 'scripts'. Repeat for more. |  |

## modelbump ask

Send prompts to a model and print the answers (to try the runner).

```text
modelbump ask [OPTIONS] PROMPTS
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `PROMPTS` | What to ask the model. Give several to ask them all. | required |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--model`, `-m` | endpoint/model, e.g. ollama/qwen2.5:7b. | `ollama/qwen2.5:7b` |
| `--system` | A system message. |  |
| `--temperature` | Sampling temperature. | `0.0` |
| `--max-tokens` | Longest answer, in tokens. |  |
| `--seed` | Sampling seed, if the model supports it. |  |
| `--sample` | Which repeated draw this is (0, 1, 2, ...). | `0` |
| `--timeout` | Seconds each attempt may take. | `120.0` |
| `--attempts` | Tries before giving up. | `4` |
| `--cache`, `--no-cache` | Reuse a stored answer to the same request. | on |
| `--budget-tokens` | Stop sending requests after this many tokens (in + out). |  |
| `--budget-requests` | Stop after this many requests to the model, retries included. |  |
| `--think` | Reasoning effort for thinking models: none, low, medium or high. Leave it out for the model's default. |  |

## modelbump models

List the models pulled into Ollama, with the digest that pins each one.

```text
modelbump models
```

## modelbump cache info

Show where the cache is and how much it holds.

```text
modelbump cache info
```

## modelbump cache clear

Delete every stored answer.

```text
modelbump cache clear [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--yes`, `-y` | Do not ask for confirmation. | off |

## modelbump repair show

Show what a patch changes in each test case, without asking any model.

Exits with 2 when the patch does not fit the suite.

```text
modelbump repair show SUITE_FILE PATCH_FILE
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `SUITE_FILE` | The suite file from `modelbump suite`. | required |
| `PATCH_FILE` | The patch file to check. | required |

## modelbump repair propose

Ask a model for candidate patches for every call with a REGRESSED case (ADR 0063).

Each candidate is a patch file you can check with `repair show` and test with `modelbump test --patch`. Nothing here says a candidate works. The naive and iterative strategies are the baselines of ADR 0065; iterative also asks the old and new models from the report, to score its candidates.

```text
modelbump repair propose [OPTIONS] SUITE_FILE REPORT_FILE
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `SUITE_FILE` | The suite file from `modelbump suite`. | required |
| `REPORT_FILE` | A `modelbump test --format json` report of that suite, run without a patch. | required |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--model` | The model that writes candidate patches, as endpoint/model. | `ollama/gemma3:12b` |
| `--candidates` | Answers asked per call; each can give one candidate. | `5` |
| `--output-dir` | Folder for the candidate patch files and proposals.json. | `modelbump-proposals` |
| `--strategy` | evidence (from the failing answers), or the baselines naive and iterative. | `evidence` |
| `--rounds` | iterative: rounds of proposals. | `3` |
| `--per-round` | iterative: proposals per round. | `2` |
| `--screen-runs` | iterative: answers per case to score each candidate. | `10` |
| `--from-think` | iterative: reasoning effort for the old model, if the report has none. |  |
| `--to-think` | iterative: reasoning effort for the new model, e.g. none for Qwen 3. |  |

## modelbump repair run

Screen the candidate patches, confirm the best on fresh answers, keep only safe ones.

A patch is accepted only if, on every test case of its call, the patched new model is shown to be no more than --margin worse than the old model (ADR 0064). Exits with 1 when a call could not be repaired.

```text
modelbump repair run [OPTIONS] SUITE_FILE PROPOSALS
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `SUITE_FILE` | The suite file from `modelbump suite`. | required |
| `PROPOSALS` | The folder `modelbump repair propose` wrote. | required |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--from` | The model the app uses now, as endpoint/model. | required |
| `--to` | The model to move to, as endpoint/model. | required |
| `--screen-runs` | Answers per case for each candidate when screening. | `10` |
| `--confirm-runs` | Fresh answers per model per case when confirming. | `100` |
| `--confirm-top` | Best candidates to confirm per call (alpha is split among them). | `1` |
| `--alpha` | Chance per call of accepting a patch that breaks a case. | `0.05` |
| `--margin` | How much worse than the old model still counts as fine. | `0.1` |
| `--max-gap` | Do not confirm a candidate that screens this far below the old model. | `0.25` |
| `--reference` | Old-model answers per case that set the reference (not scored). | `3` |
| `--from-think` | Reasoning effort for the --from model: none, low, medium or high. |  |
| `--to-think` | Reasoning effort for the --to model, e.g. none for Qwen 3. |  |
| `--temperature` | Sampling temperature for both models. | `0.7` |
| `--max-tokens` | Longest answer, in tokens. | `400` |
| `--judge` | The model that judges free-text answers, as endpoint/model. | `ollama/gemma3:12b` |
| `--no-judge` | Check free text with property checks only. | off |
| `--budget-requests` | Stop after this many requests (cached answers are free). |  |
| `--output` | Patch file for the accepted patches. | `modelbump-repair.json` |
| `--report` | Also write the full JSON report to this file. |  |

## modelbump judge sheet

Write a blind sheet of judged answers for you to label PASS or FAIL.

```text
modelbump judge sheet [OPTIONS] REPORT
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `REPORT` | A `modelbump test --format json` report. | required |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--output` | The blind sheet to label (CSV). | `judge-sheet.csv` |
| `--key` | What the sheet hides: models and judge verdicts. | `judge-key.json` |
| `--size` | Answers to draw, half judged PASS, half FAIL. | `200` |
| `--seed` | Seed for drawing and shuffling. | `2030` |
| `--exclude-key` | Leave out the answers of an earlier sheet's key. Repeat for more. |  |

## modelbump judge agreement

How often the judge agrees with your labels, and pass rates corrected for it.

```text
modelbump judge agreement [OPTIONS] SHEET KEY
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `SHEET` | The labelled sheet (CSV). | required |
| `KEY` | The key from `modelbump judge sheet`. | required |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--report` | Compare with this report's verdicts instead (the same run, judged again). |  |

## modelbump judge probes

Break reference answers on purpose, judge them, and write a blind sheet to check.

```text
modelbump judge probes [OPTIONS] REPORT
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `REPORT` | A `modelbump test --format json` report. | required |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--output` | The blind probe sheet to label (CSV). | `probe-sheet.csv` |
| `--key` | What the sheet hides: each probe's kind and verdict. | `probe-key.json` |
| `--breaker` | The model that writes the probes, as endpoint/model. | `ollama/qwen2.5:7b` |
| `--judge` | The judge to test, as endpoint/model. | `ollama/gemma3:12b` |
| `--per-kind` | Probes of each kind per free-text case. | `2` |
| `--seed` | Seed for shuffling the sheet. | `2032` |
| `--budget-requests` | Stop after this many requests (cached answers are free). |  |

## modelbump judge probe-check

Which kinds of broken answer the judge catches, checked against your labels.

```text
modelbump judge probe-check SHEET KEY
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `SHEET` | The labelled probe sheet (CSV). | required |
| `KEY` | The key from `modelbump judge probes`. | required |

## modelbump stats item

Compare pass counts of the old and new model on one test case.

```text
modelbump stats item [OPTIONS] OLD NEW
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `OLD` | Old model's passes/runs, for example 9/10. | required |
| `NEW` | New model's passes/runs, for example 4/10. | required |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--margin` | Largest change in pass rate that still counts as the same (0.1 = 10 points). | `0.1` |
| `--alpha` | Chance of a wrong REGRESSED, IMPROVED or EQUIVALENT claim. | `0.05` |

## modelbump stats simulate

Pretend two models answer one test case, and stop as soon as the verdict is clear.

```text
modelbump stats simulate [OPTIONS] OLD_RATE NEW_RATE
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `OLD_RATE` | Old model's true pass rate, e.g. 0.9. | required |
| `NEW_RATE` | New model's true pass rate, e.g. 0.6. | required |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--seed` | Random seed, so a run can be repeated. | `1` |
| `--max-runs` | Stop with INCONCLUSIVE after this many answers per model. | `200` |
| `--margin` | Largest change in pass rate that still counts as the same (0.1 = 10 points). | `0.1` |
| `--alpha` | Chance of a wrong REGRESSED, IMPROVED or EQUIVALENT claim. | `0.05` |
| `--scores` | Answers get a score between 0 and 1 with these means, not pass/fail. | off |

## modelbump stats simulate-suite

Pretend two models answer a whole suite, and control false alarms across it.

```text
modelbump stats simulate-suite [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--items` | Test cases in the suite. | `300` |
| `--regressed` | How many test cases the new model is really worse on. | `30` |
| `--drop` | How much pass rate those test cases lose (0.3 = 30 points). | `0.3` |
| `--seed` | Random seed, so a run can be repeated. | `1` |
| `--fdr` | Largest expected share of false alarms among REGRESSED. | `0.05` |
| `--max-runs` | Stop a test case with INCONCLUSIVE after this many answers. | `200` |
| `--margin` | Largest change in pass rate that still counts as the same (0.1 = 10 points). | `0.1` |
| `--futility` | Stop a test case that looks fine once its REGRESSED evidence falls below this (e.g. 0.1), after 20 answers. |  |
